title: Gallery renditions - size-matched image thumbs and a video proxy
description: The gallery renders ONE 512px image thumb at every card size, and promotes video to the FULL-RESOLUTION master. At the biggest card size the thumb is visibly upscaled (Fabio: 'they look like shit'), which pushes users into the History workspace just to see their own asset; and a 3000x1280 clip in a ~300px card decodes ~100x more pixels than the card shows. Add size-matched image renditions picked by RENDERED box (not items-per-row), and a small video proxy for gallery hover playback. Full-res stays in the viewer.
acceptance: A card picks the SMALLEST rendition whose pixels meet or exceed its RENDERED box, falling back to the original when no rendition is big enough - never a fixed tier keyed to the slider level

Sizing keys off the rendered pixel box (max of width and height), NOT items-per-row: with justified rows, three PORTRAIT cards per row are narrow but tall, so a column count does not tell you how many pixels the card actually paints
No rendition is generated larger than its source - most assets here are 1280x800, so a large card should simply use the original rather than an upscaled derivative
Video promotes to a small proxy (720p, or 480p - Fabio: either is fine) for gallery hover playback; the viewer still opens the full-res master
Renditions are generated by the existing services/ffmpegThumb.js (extractImageThumb already takes a width option) using the bundled ffmpeg - no new dependency
Existing projects backfill, following the MPI-319 pattern (POST /backfill-image-thumbs, fired fire-and-forget on project load, patching live items + rebuilding the grid)
Renditions live and die with the sidecar, on the same GC as the existing thumbs, and the GC/delete paths accept every extension in use

Alpha survives every image rendition - WebP, never JPG (MPI-627: a JPG thumb of a background-removed PNG hands back the ORIGINAL image whole, backdrop included, and the card then disagrees with the viewer)

Measured: gallery VRAM at the LARGEST card size is not materially worse than at the smallest - the screen's pixel count is fixed, so counts and sizes should cancel; a regression here means the tier selection is wrong
Measured: per-video decode cost against resolution, so the proxy's size is chosen on evidence rather than the reasoning in brief.md
docs/gallery.md documents the rendition ladder and the selection rule; UNRELEASED.md gets an entry
